alignments.note: τε keeps whatever connective the ASV writes for it; rule 70. No answering καί stands in the verse.
Supplied subordinator when on a participle is an ordinary rule 7 helper under rule 86, discontinuously under rule 15.
Article takes the English determiner; rule 19.
The ASV renders the plural ὄχλοι by the collective singular multitude.
Relative pronoun aligned to what.
Subject name of the relative clause.
Auxiliary rides with the lexical verb; rule 9.
The particle up realizes the preverb ἐπ- and rides inside the verb's unit with its supplied subject; rule 106, headed on the verb word.
Determiner slot displaced by the possessive their, which belongs to αὐτῶν; rule 20.

The adverb Λυκαονιστί is expanded into the frame in the speech of Lycaonia; the ethnonym is what glosses the stem and speech is the supplied generic completion, so the head is Lycaonia under rules 17 and 66. No Greek preposition or determiner-bearing article stands, so the whole frame rides with the adverb under rule 67.
Article takes the English determiner; rule 19.
Head noun of the articular phrase.
The particle down realizes the preverb κατα- and the auxiliary are rides with the verb; rule 106, headed on the verb word.
Preposition aligned to to.
Accusative pronoun aligned to us.

The participle is recast as the nominal frame in the likeness of, whose supplied noun likeness is what licenses the of; rule 21's frame clause keeps that preposition inside the verb's own unit, exactly as ἀναμνήσει … τὰς ὁδούς μου → shall put you in remembrance of my ways does, and rule 27 forbids splitting a helper from what licenses it. A dative's own case is realized in English by to, unto or with, so of answers to no case of ἀνθρώποις. Head on likeness, the word glossing ὁμοι-. Giving of men to the dative under rule 21's ordinary case-preposition clause remains defensible.
The governed word keeps a bare noun, the frame's supplied likeness having taken the of; rule 21.

review_notes: Corrected: of men no longer sits on ἀνθρώποις. The of is licensed by the frame noun likeness rather than by the dative — a dative's own case is realized by to, unto or with — so rule 21's frame clause keeps it inside the participle's unit and the governed word stands as a bare men, on the model of ἀναμνήσει … τὰς ὁδούς μου → shall put you in remembrance of my ways. The competing reading is named in that unit's note.
Λυκαονιστί is headed on Lycaonia rather than on speech, speech being the supplied generic completion under rule 17's generic-noun clause, with rule 66's compound test agreeing.
Both variants here are underdetermined with base readings compatible with the ASV, so no rule 97 note is owed.
